description: Rhodes electric piano listing copy, organized by model, production era, and cabinet type, plus a cosmetic add-on snippet library.

nodes.label: 1960's Sparkletop
nodes.copy:
Every Rhodes we restore for sale receives our highest level of craftsmanship, with over 30 hours dedicated to bringing it to exceptional playing condition. Our process goes beyond the original factory setup, carefully preserving the instrument's iconic tone while addressing any of the wear and tear that it has experienced over the decades. Throughout the restoration we prioritize period-correct vintage components whenever possible, or select the highest-quality reproduction parts when necessary to bring out the best of the Rhodes while staying true to the sound of its production year. Finally, the instrument receives a setup more detailed than its original factory setup, ensuring that it is ready to be enjoyed for decades more to come.

This is a 1960's Rhodes "Sparkletop," a vibey and percussive piano shaped by its Raymac tines and felt hammers — the same bark heard on The Beatles' "Let It Be," Quincy Jones' "Walking in Space," and Miles Davis' "Bitches Brew." Rhodes was still refining the instrument's design during this era, so pianos from this period sit closer to prototypes for what would become the Mark I.

Features:
- New Tone Bar Suspension Grommets
- New Hammer Tips
- Fully Restored Key Bed and Action Regulation
- New Bushing Felts
- CEPCo's Expert Tuning & Voicing Setup
- New Electrolytic Capacitors
- Fully Restored Power Supply
- Low Noise
- Cleaned All Potentiometers and Connectors
- All Voltages Checked, Offset & Bias set at Optimum Performance
- New Neutrik+Mogami Cables

Included:
- Legs
- Sustain Pedal

Finally, the instrument receives a setup more detailed than its original factory setup, ensuring that it is ready to be enjoyed for decades more to come.

This piano comes from the early Mark I period (1971-1973), after Rhodes worked out the quirks of the Sparkletop era and switched to neoprene hammer tips, which were used for the rest of Rhodes production. The thick, cube-shaped hammer tips paired with Torrington tines give this era its tone: a thick, dark thump in the bass and a sparkly, bright attack in the treble. This is the barkiest of all Rhodes eras, heard on early Stevie Wonder records, Chick Corea's Return to Forever, and many more.

This is a Stage piano — it does not include a built-in amplifier or speakers, so it pairs with an external amp or PA. Stage pianos also lack the onboard vibrato/tremolo circuit found on Suitcase models.

This piano comes from the later Torrington-tine period (1974-1976), when a new batch of tines produced a slightly more balanced and warm bark than the earlier Mark I. Expect deep, warm bass, barky midrange, and a touch less bright attack in the treble compared to 1971-1973 pianos. Rhodes changed its branding from "Fender Rhodes" to "Rhodes" in mid-1974, though this was a change in name only — the hammer tips and tines from this era carried through into 1976.

This is a Stage piano — it does not include a built-in amplifier or speakers, so it pairs with an external amp or PA. Stage pianos also lack the onboard vibrato/tremolo circuit found on Suitcase models.

children.copy:
Every Rhodes we restore for sale receives our highest level of craftsmanship, with over 30 hours dedicated to bringing it to exceptional playing condition. Our process goes beyond the original factory setup, carefully preserving the instrument's iconic tone while addressing any of the wear and tear that it has experienced over the decades. Throughout the restoration we prioritize period-correct vintage components whenever possible, or select the highest-quality reproduction parts when necessary to bring out the best of the Rhodes while staying true to the sound of its production year. Finally, the instrument receives a setup more detailed than its original factory setup, ensuring that it is ready to be enjoyed for decades more to come.

This piano uses Schaller tines, the tine type used from 1978 through the last Mark II's built in 1983. Pianos from this era are the most harmonically balanced across the keyboard, known for a bell-like treble and upper midrange.

This is a Suitcase piano, which includes a built-in power amp, stereo speakers, and Rhodes' factory vibrato/tremolo circuit, so it's ready to play on its own without an external amp.
